pairs.source_text: May a model verify, rule, seal, or publish?
pairs.target_text:
no - a model may propose; only a person may verify, rule, seal, or publish

Reason: the fleet's most load-bearing principle exists everywhere as prose (CLAUDE.md 0.2, intake_desk_spec 4.1, promote_check verified_by != author, Nestor's seal, the fourth-store narrative) and nowhere as a sealed decision - found by asking Nestor, which correctly answered that nobody ever sealed it. The intake desk paid the tuition: a router with a careful vocabulary contract still emitted unearned conclusions through the middle of it, because every rule was about storage and none was about authorship.
Record: docs/specs/intake_desk_spec.md 4.1; CLAUDE.md 0.2; stores/promote_check.py; docs/the-fourth-store.md; prior art found at reconciliation: willow-gate custody-ledger-spec header, 2026-07-11 - 'author: instance (proposes; operator ratifies)... nothing here is built without operator ratification'
Sealed by: rudi193 (2026-08-05)
pairs.source_norm: may a model verify rule seal or publish

pairs.source_text: May a subject's testimony be published attributed under their name?
pairs.target_text:
only under its own explicit scope (testimony_publication) - granting it never implies kb_promotion, and granting kb_promotion never implies it

Reason: attributed testimony and de-identified structure are opposite movements: an oral-history desk publishes the naming as the record ('Names Given Not Chosen') while kb_promotion strips identity for a shared index - one consent must never quietly stand in for the other
Record: libs/subject-consent core.py (the scope's own comment); apps/intake-desk; reconciled 2026-08-05: willow-gate H2 supplies the enforcement FRAME (three-key model: capability + consent + unexpired lease) but not this rule - the scope-independence of testimony_publication vs kb_promotion is genuinely new law.
Sealed by: rudi193 (2026-08-05)
pairs.source_norm: may a subjects testimony be published attributed under their name

pairs.source_text: May the field recording why a boundary was crossed be free text?
pairs.target_text:
no - a closed set for writers, pinned by a test, permissive for readers

Reason: convergent law: three sessions fixed this same defect independently in one night (homestead R-7 and I-13, Nestor #32 closed by #33, willow-mcp #280's event_type note) - a control nothing can check is a label, and a typo'd kind is not an event type, it is a row silently absent from every review surface
Record: nestor PR #33; homestead R-7/I-13; willow-mcp #280
Sealed by: rudi193 (2026-08-05)

pairs.source_text: Must a declared purpose be checkable rather than a label?
pairs.target_text:
yes - a declared purpose is a control, and a control nothing can check is a label

Reason: homestead's Purpose accepted any non-blank string, so 'x' bought the same lift as 'medical'; the fleet-level generalization is that any declaration which grants reach must be enforceable at the point it grants it
Record: homestead invariant I-13; PRIOR ART CONFIRMED (reconciled 2026-08-05): willow-gate's founding rule - 'trust is not asserted, it is bound... Elder is not a text field anyone can type' (README), check-out reconciles declared against observed, and hardening H2 demotes the text-scan to advisory in favor of a checkable lease. This entry is the fleet-level statement of willow-gate's law.
Sealed by: rudi193 (2026-08-05)
pairs.source_norm: must a declared purpose be checkable rather than a label

pairs.source_text: Must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database?
pairs.target_text:
yes - hold verify()'s head somewhere the chain's writer cannot reach, and pass it back as expected_head

Reason: rechain() proves the migration and the forgery are the same operation, so internal consistency alone can never answer 'is this the same chain it was yesterday'; a mirror without an external anchor degrades from 'someone else remembers' to 'someone else has a copy that will agree with whatever it now says'
Record: willow-mcp #280, PR #281; nestor ledger's expected_head precedent; prior art found at reconciliation: willow-gate custody-ledger-spec, 2026-07-11 - 'the ledger is the authority; the file is not... the lock lives where the handled thing cannot reach it', with the signed sidecar explicitly labeled weaker (authenticity, never completeness) - the rechain-marker bound, stated three weeks early
Sealed by: rudi193 (2026-08-05)
pairs.source_norm: must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database

pairs.source_text: Should source code be eliminated in favor of AI-generated binaries? — option: generate efficient binaries directly, no source intermediate
pairs.target_text:
REJECTED. destroys the witness layer: source is the record, not the instructions - the only medium in which a second human can check the first; a model's derivation is neither deterministic nor reproducible, and opacity pools trust in whoever runs the model
Reopen when: generation becomes deterministic, reproducible, and auditable end to end
Verified by: rudi193
pairs.source_norm: should source code be eliminated in favor of aigenerated binaries option generate efficient binaries directly no source intermediate

Reopen when: never
Verified by: rudi193
